Package neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline

Class PigMotion

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.PigMotion
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class PigMotion extends Object implements Serializable
Experimental rigid-pig mechanics under prescribed, piecewise-constant pressure and inclination.

Positive position and velocity follow the pipe coordinate. Pressure differential is upstream minus downstream pressure in Pa; inclination is positive uphill in radians. The applied force is area * deltaP - mass * g * sin(inclination). Static friction holds a resting pig through equality with its specified breakaway force. Moving friction opposes velocity. A zero-velocity event is resolved exactly before deciding whether to stick or reverse. No velocity floor, time-step-dependent friction or empirical pig parameters are supplied.

This stateless submodel does not solve fluid inventories, bypass, pressure waves, pig receipt, bends or changing diameter. Callers must split steps at prescribed pressure/geometry changes. A future hydraulic coupling must balance the pressure work and displaced volume on both sides of the pig; prescribing pressure here does not provide that coupling.

  • Method Details

    • advance

      public PigMotion.Step advance(double positionM, double velocityMps, double differentialPressurePa, double inclinationRadians, double durationSeconds)
      Advances the mechanical state analytically through one constant-input interval.
      Parameters:
      positionM - initial axial position in m; signed coordinates are allowed
      velocityMps - initial signed axial velocity in m/s
      differentialPressurePa - upstream minus downstream pressure in Pa
      inclinationRadians - pipe angle from horizontal in radians, in [-pi/2, pi/2]
      durationSeconds - interval duration in s, nonnegative
      Returns:
      immutable motion and mechanical work ledger for this interval

    • simulate

      public PigMotion.Trajectory simulate(double positionM, double velocityMps, double[] durationsSeconds, double[] pressureDifferencesPa, double[] inclinationsRadians)
      Runs a prescribed schedule, splitting exactly at every input event.

      Inclination is prescribed in time, not looked up from a spatial route. This method cannot detect arrival at a receiver or a terrain breakpoint. Returned samples include the initial state and every interval endpoint.

      Parameters:
      positionM - initial axial position in m
      velocityMps - initial axial velocity in m/s
      durationsSeconds - nonempty positive interval durations in s
      pressureDifferencesPa - pressure differentials in Pa, one per interval
      inclinationsRadians - inclinations in radians, one per interval
      Returns:
      immutable trajectory with mechanical ledgers and defensive sample arrays
